chunk_findings.detail: The new `_next_token(...)` call carries only `kind`, `phase`, `phase_only`, and `tags`; it does not pass the `wave` filter that the change states it must carry. As written, a run such as `ddflow next --wave 3` cut by `[output].max_rows` produces a next-page footer without `--wave 3`, so the printed cursor is applied to the list without the wave filter, reproducing the dropped-filter bug for wave.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: The stated fix says the non-lane `next` token must carry wave as well as phase/kind/phase_only/tag, but neither the parser nor the token builder has any wave handling: `_next_flags` only recognizes `--kind`, `--phase`, `--phase-only`, and `--tag`, and `next_token` has no `wave` parameter or `--wave` output. Given a wave-narrowed non-lane next command such as `next --wave 1 --phase P`, `_next_flags` ignores `--wave`, `_entry` returns `ddflow next --phase P`, and `_page_calls` prints the page footer as `ddflow next --phase P --cursor 50`. The next page is therefore filtered by phase but not by wave, so it can include tasks from other waves, reproducing the paging-drops-filters bug for wave filters. If `next_token` is intended to carry a separate wave filter, its current signature `(kind, phase, phase_only, tags=())` cannot express it without callers misusing `tags`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_next_flags / next_token

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test exercises `phase`, `kind`, `tag`, and `phase_only`, but it never exercises `wave`, even though the stated fix carries `wave` in the command token. A regression that drops `--wave` / `wave=` from the next-page token would pass this test. For example, if `_next_flags` emits `--wave 3` today but later changes to omit `wave` unless some other filter is present, the token for `ddflow next --phase P-coordination --wave 3` cut by `max_rows` would page the wrong unfiltered-by-wave list, while this test still passes because no `_nonlane_footer` call supplies `wave` and no assertion checks the wave flag.
